newsitem.title: USA: Solv-Ex Corp may file for Chapter 11.
newsitem.headline: Solv-Ex Corp may file for Chapter 11.

text.p: Solv-Ex Corp said Monday it could seek protection under Chapter 11 bankruptcy if necessary while it tries to restructure an overall plan of action for its Northern Alberta oil sands project.

The company said it has filed a petition in Canada to stay actions by creditors against the project, for which the company had been seeking additional financing. Additional financing for the project fell through after a drop in the company's share price, said Solv-Ex Chairman John Randall.

"The current situation arose because of a number of factors, including having proceeded with plant modifications and limited operations with the expectation that additional financing would be in place," a company statement said.
It said liens totalling about $3.5 million have been filed against the property and there are additional unsecured claims of about $7.3 million in Canada and $1 million in the U.S.

Randall said the company hopes the Canadian filing would allow sufficient time to develop an alternative plan for the project, which has already been successfully demonstrated to several prospective partners, he said.
"We're trying to put an alternative plan of action in place, and it depends on various factors to determine what the next move is," Randall said.
The company may also seek similar protection in the U.S. against its creditors. "It's possible. We have not yet made that decision," Senior Vice President Herb Campbell said.
In the meantime, plant operations are being cut and security guards are on site until financing can be completed, the company said.
